texts: Opening the floor of the pericardial reflection in the transverse sinus provides the most direct avenue for rerouting the collaterals: C.
Through it, collaterals from the descending aorta behind the heart can be brought forward to the central pulmonary arteries by the shortest path.
The pleurae are opened behind the phrenic nerves, the native pulmonary arteries are fully mobilized, and the collaterals are controlled before bypass starts to avoid flooding the lungs.
Most of the unifocalization is done on bypass with the heart beating, without cross-clamping.
In the picture, Franky brings every treasure-map path through the opened floor of the tunnel behind the orca and the money pipe.
Memory hook: the paths come forward through the floor of the tunnel behind the heart.
